title: Cloud Marketplace SKU Catalog & Packaging Proposal (v2)
author: Nikhil Sharma
body:
## Summary
This document defines the proposed **v2 SKU catalog** for AWS Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace, aligned to Redwood’s product lines:
- **Hosted API (usage-based)**
- **Dedicated capacity (reserved/contracted)**
- **Private deployment (license + support)**
- **Add-ons** (compliance, retention, premium support/SLA)

It also defines **naming conventions**, **entitlement identifiers**, **mapping to internal plans/metering**, and **initial pricing guardrails** for Finance + Sales alignment.

**Non-goals:** final price books, full billing re-platforming, or new runtime functionality.

---

## Goals
1) Make it easy for enterprise buyers to purchase Redwood through cloud marketplaces with procurement-friendly terms.
2) Ensure SKUs map cleanly to:
   - Redwood org entitlements
   - internal plan codes
   - billing meters / invoice descriptions
   - regional availability & routing policies
3) Reduce ambiguity across AWS vs GCP listings (consistent taxonomy and add-on semantics).
4) Create guardrails for discounting and packaging so Sales/Finance can maintain margin while meeting marketplace constraints.

---

## Marketplace packaging principles
**P1. Keep base SKUs simple; move complexity to add-ons.**
- Hosted should be “pay for what you use” (tokens/embeddings) with a small number of tiers.
- Dedicated should be expressed as a small set of **capacity bundles** rather than bespoke GPU counts.
- Private should be a **platform license** with explicit support tier.

**P2. Naming must be consistent across: marketplace listing title, console plan name, internal plan code, and entitlement IDs.**

**P3. Separate “commercial construct” from “technical deployment mode.”**
- A marketplace purchase creates entitlements and billing relationships.
- The underlying deployment could still be multi-region, VPC, or on-prem depending on the SKU.

**P4. Add-ons must be attachable across product lines where possible.**
- Compliance and retention add-ons should apply to Hosted/Dedicated/Private unless technically impossible.

---

## Naming conventions (v2)
### SKU display name format (customer-facing)
**Redwood Inference — <Product Line> — <Tier/Bundle> (<Billing Construct>)**

Examples:
- “Redwood Inference — Hosted API — Standard (Usage)”
- “Redwood Inference — Dedicated — Pro Bundle (Monthly)”
- “Redwood Inference — Private — Enterprise License (Annual)”
- “Redwood Inference — Compliance Pack (Add-on)”

### Internal plan code format
**MP_<PROVIDER>_<PRODUCT>_<TIER_OR_BUNDLE>_<BILLING>_V2**

Examples:
- MP_AWS_HOSTED_STANDARD_USAGE_V2
- MP_GCP_DEDICATED_PRO_MONTHLY_V2

### Entitlement ID format (technical)
**ent.mp.<provider>.<product>.<tier_or_bundle>[.<addon>]**

Rules:
- Entitlement IDs are stable; listing copy can evolve.
- Add-ons are separate entitlements, not “hidden features.”

---

## SKU catalog (v2)
The tables below define the canonical v2 SKU set. Provider-specific constraints (e.g., packaging rules, metering implementation differences) are documented in the “AWS vs GCP notes” section.

### A) Hosted API (Usage-based)
**What the buyer gets:** token-based access to Hosted API endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank where enabled), with org-level quotas + usage analytics.

| SKU (display) | Marketplace construct | Intended buyer | Included | Not included | Internal plan code | Entitlement IDs | Billing meters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted API — Starter (Usage) | Usage-based | Self-serve + small teams; procurement wants marketplace record | Hosted API access, basic analytics, standard support | Premium SLA, extended retention, compliance pack | MP_<PROVIDER>_HOSTED_STARTER_USAGE_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.hosted.starter | meter.tokens.input, meter.tokens.output, meter.embeddings.units |
| Hosted API — Standard (Usage) | Usage-based | Default for most marketplace buyers | Same as Starter + higher default quotas | Premium SLA, extended retention, compliance pack | MP_<PROVIDER>_HOSTED_STANDARD_USAGE_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.hosted.standard | meter.tokens.input, meter.tokens.output, meter.embeddings.units |
| Hosted API — Enterprise (Contract / Private Offer) | Contracted (provider-specific) | Enterprise procurement requiring commit + invoicing | Same as Standard, negotiated quotas, assisted onboarding | Dedicated capacity (separate SKU), Private control plane (separate SKU) | MP_<PROVIDER>_HOSTED_ENTERPRISE_CONTRACT_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.hosted.enterprise | meter.tokens.input, meter.tokens.output, meter.embeddings.units (with commit) |

Notes:
- Hosted API SKUs are **model-catalog agnostic**; access is governed by Redwood policy + region availability.
- If a customer requires strict data isolation or VPC networking, route them to **Dedicated** or **Private**.


### B) Dedicated capacity (Reserved bundles)
**What the buyer gets:** dedicated GPU pool(s) with predictable throughput and data isolation, billed as a recurring commitment (monthly/annual depending on provider support).

Bundle sizing is intentionally coarse; bespoke sizing should be done via direct contract unless the marketplace supports private offers with custom dimensions.

| SKU (display) | Marketplace construct | Target workloads | Included | Not included | Internal plan code | Entitlement IDs | Primary meters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dedicated — Team Bundle (Monthly) | Subscription / contract | Department / pilot in production | 1 dedicated pool (baseline capacity), standard uptime target, basic onboarding | Premium SLA, compliance pack, extended retention | MP_<PROVIDER>_DEDICATED_TEAM_MONTHLY_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.dedicated.team | meter.dedicated.capacity_units |
| Dedicated — Pro Bundle (Monthly) | Subscription / contract | Production apps with latency SLOs | Larger pool, autoscaling policy options, priority support queue | Private on-prem package | MP_<PROVIDER>_DEDICATED_PRO_MONTHLY_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.dedicated.pro | meter.dedicated.capacity_units |
| Dedicated — Enterprise Bundle (Annual) | Contract / private offer | Enterprise platform teams | Multi-pool option, enterprise onboarding, enhanced support response targets (if Premium SLA add-on attached) | Private license | MP_<PROVIDER>_DEDICATED_ENTERPRISE_ANNUAL_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.dedicated.enterprise | meter.dedicated.capacity_units |

Definition: **capacity_units**
- A normalized unit representing reserved inference capacity (internally mapped to GPU type/count and region).
- This abstraction avoids tying marketplace SKUs to specific GPU SKUs that change frequently.


### C) Private deployment (License + support)
**What the buyer gets:** Redwood Private control plane (VPC) and/or on-prem package eligibility, with explicit support tier.

| SKU (display) | Marketplace construct | Intended buyer | Included | Not included | Internal plan code | Entitlement IDs | Meter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Private — Business License (Annual) | Annual contract / private offer | Regulated teams needing VPC + control plane isolation | Private control plane entitlement, install artifacts access, standard support | Premium SLA, compliance pack (separate), custom security work | MP_<PROVIDER>_PRIVATE_BUSINESS_ANNUAL_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.private.business | meter.private.license |
| Private — Enterprise License (Annual) | Annual contract / private offer | Regulated + large deployments | Private entitlement + enterprise support baseline, onboarding workshop | Premium SLA (recommended add-on), compliance pack | MP_<PROVIDER>_PRIVATE_ENTERPRISE_ANNUAL_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.private.enterprise | meter.private.license |

Notes:
- Private SKUs are **license-oriented**; usage charges (tokens) are not metered via marketplace by default.
- If a provider requires a usage dimension for listing eligibility, we will meter a zero-rated “activation dimension” (Finance to confirm acceptability).


### D) Add-ons (attachable entitlements)
Add-ons are separate SKUs and entitlements to preserve clarity and enable clean upgrades.

| Add-on SKU (display) | Applies to | Included capabilities | Internal plan code | Entitlement ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compliance Pack (Add-on) | Hosted + Dedicated + Private | Audit log access (console/API), configurable retention controls (where supported), security documentation bundle access workflow, compliance-friendly defaults | MP_<PROVIDER>_ADDON_COMPLIANCE_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.addon.compliance |
| Observability Retention — 30d (Add-on) | Hosted + Dedicated | Extended metrics/traces retention in Console | MP_<PROVIDER>_ADDON_OBS_RETENTION_30D_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.addon.obs_retention_30d |
| Observability Retention — 90d (Add-on) | Hosted + Dedicated | Same as above (90 days) | MP_<PROVIDER>_ADDON_OBS_RETENTION_90D_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.addon.obs_retention_90d |
| Premium SLA (Add-on) | Dedicated + Private (and Hosted Enterprise only) | Higher support response targets, SLA language alignment, escalation routing | MP_<PROVIDER>_ADDON_PREMIUM_SLA_V2 | ent.mp.<provider>.addon.premium_sla |

Add-on constraints:
- Premium SLA cannot be purchased without an eligible base SKU (Dedicated/Private/Hosted Enterprise).
- Compliance Pack can be purchased standalone for procurement reasons, but requires an active base SKU to activate controls.

---

## Mapping to Redwood internal product entitlements
### Canonical entitlement set (provider-agnostic)
Internally we map provider-specific entitlements to canonical Redwood entitlements used by Console gating:
- hosted_api_access
- dedicated_capacity_access
- private_deployment_access
- addon_compliance
- addon_obs_retention_30d
- addon_obs_retention_90d
- addon_premium_sla

Provider-specific entitlements (e.g., ent.mp.aws.hosted.standard) must map 1:1 into this canonical set with a tier attribute.

### Tier-to-feature mapping (high-level)
Hosted tiers differ primarily by:
- default quotas
- support routing priority (not SLA)
- eligibility for private offers and invoicing terms

Dedicated and Private tiers differ primarily by:
- support baseline
- onboarding included
- contract term shape (monthly vs annual)

---

## Initial pricing guidance & guardrails (v2)
This section defines guardrails, not the final list price. Final numbers are maintained in Finance’s marketplace model and the provider portals.

### 1) Hosted API usage rates
Guidance:
- Maintain parity with (or a small premium to) direct self-serve pricing to account for marketplace fees.
- Keep a clear input vs output token rate structure.

Guardrails:
- **Floor price:** do not go below the approved “Marketplace Floor” for token meters (see Finance model). Any exception requires approval from **Laura Bennett** and **Jordan Blake**.
- **Discounting:** avoid “hidden discounts” via custom meters. Use private offers/commits where supported.
- **Commit policy:** Hosted Enterprise via marketplace should be offered as commit-based (annual preferred) when customer requires invoicing/PO.

### 2) Dedicated bundles
Guidance:
- Dedicated should be priced as a capacity commitment with predictable invoice lines.
- Prefer 3 bundles (Team / Pro / Enterprise) rather than many GPU-specific SKUs.

Guardrails:
- **Minimum term:** monthly for Team/Pro; annual for Enterprise (unless provider constraints force uniformity).
- **Bundle change policy:** upgrades allowed mid-term via add-on / amendment; downgrades effective next renewal (see Upgrade/Downgrade policy).
- **Margin protection:** marketplace fee impact must be baked into list; do not “match direct” on net price without private offer approval.

### 3) Private license
Guidance:
- Private should remain annual (or multi-year) and routed through private offers.

Guardrails:
- Private via marketplace is for procurement channel preference, not for discounting.
- Ensure invoice descriptors clearly separate “license” from “support” where provider allows line-item descriptions.

### 4) Add-ons
Guidance:
- Add-ons should be easy to attach to a base SKU and should not materially change technical provisioning steps.

Guardrails:
- Observability retention add-ons should be priced to cover storage + operational cost.
- Premium SLA should be priced to reflect support load and must require exec sponsor sign-off on the support commitments.

---

## Upgrade / downgrade policy (proposal)
This policy is intended to minimize support issues and revenue leakage.

**Hosted (usage tiers):**
- Upgrade: immediate (entitlement change same day).
- Downgrade: next billing cycle (or next contract renewal for Enterprise).

**Dedicated (bundle):**
- Upgrade: immediate if capacity available; otherwise queued with customer communication.
- Downgrade: only at renewal, unless explicitly allowed by a private offer.

**Private (license):**
- Upgrades (Business → Enterprise): via amendment/private offer.
- Downgrades: renewal only.

**Add-ons:**
- Attach: immediate (after entitlement ingestion).
- Remove: renewal only for contract SKUs; usage-based add-ons (if any) can be removed next billing cycle.

---

## AWS vs GCP marketplace notes
### AWS Marketplace
Assumptions:
- Hosted usage meters supported (input/output tokens, embeddings units).
- Dedicated and Private primarily via contract/private offer for enterprise procurement.

Implementation notes:
- Keep meter names stable; changes require coordinated migration to avoid reporting breaks.
- AWS entitlement ingestion must handle delayed activation; provisioning pipeline should retry and surface status in Console.

### Google Cloud Marketplace
Assumptions:
- GCP listing format may require solution deployment steps and may bias toward contract/private offer for enterprise SKUs.

Implementation notes:
- Maintain consistent SKU taxonomy even if the portal displays differently.
- Ensure region availability is explicit (to avoid region mismatch provisioning errors).

---

## Invoice / line-item description guidance
Marketplace invoice line items must be readable by procurement and AP.

Rules:
- Include product line + tier + meter type where possible.
- Avoid internal terms (e.g., “capacity_units”) in customer-facing descriptions; use “Dedicated Capacity Bundle Units”.

Examples:
- “Redwood Hosted API — Input Tokens”
- “Redwood Hosted API — Output Tokens”
- “Redwood Dedicated — Pro Bundle (Monthly)”
- “Redwood — Compliance Pack (Add-on)”

---

## Open questions / decisions needed
1) Hosted Enterprise on marketplaces: do we require a minimum annual commit across both AWS/GCP, or allow monthly commits on GCP?
2) Dedicated capacity units: confirm the v2 mapping logic for GPU family changes (e.g., H100 vs L40S) and how we communicate this to customers.
3) Private license metering: confirm whether we can list Private without a usage dimension on both providers.
4) Add-on eligibility: confirm whether Compliance Pack is technically enforceable on Hosted Starter, or whether we should require Hosted Standard+.

---

Base SKUs:
- Hosted API — Starter (Usage)
- Hosted API — Standard (Usage)
- Hosted API — Enterprise (Contract / Private Offer)
- Dedicated — Team Bundle (Monthly)
- Dedicated — Pro Bundle (Monthly)
- Dedicated — Enterprise Bundle (Annual)
- Private — Business License (Annual)
- Private — Enterprise License (Annual)

Add-ons:
- Compliance Pack
- Observability Retention — 30d
- Observability Retention — 90d
- Premium SLA
